newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse closes in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse closes in slow trade.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Tuesday 0.59 percent higher with small gains in leading stocks, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 560.19 points from 556.91 on Monday.
Oil refinery Samir traded unchanged at 280 dirhams with 26,121 shares changing hands.
"Volume of trade on Samir has been important since its introduction on the electronic trading," a broker at ABN Amro Finance said.
The exchange started last week the gradual introduction of electronic trading, with shares of four companies.
ONA group, the biggest private holding, traded at 715 dirhams, unchanged from Monday.
The day's best performer was sugar firm Cosumar, up 15 dirhams to 870 dirhams with 4,285 shares traded.
Leading stock Wafabank and Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique were up five and four dirhams respectively to 730 and 194 dirhams.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing which was listed on the bourse late in February gained eight dirhams to close at 287 dirhams. Its initial price was 230 dirhams.
"It increases in value steadily with only a very small volume traded," he said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, rose five dirhams to 670 dirhams.
Brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc fell nine dirhams to 1,800 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 85.3 million dirhams from 112 million dirhams on Monday.
